correctness.rationale: After translating each set to {0,a_i,b_i}, the character column depends only on the projection π_i(ξ)∈F_2^2. Exactly three distinct of the four possible column types give determinant ±4, so a frequency triple is a basis precisely when π_i is injective on it. The combined map has rank r and fibers of size 2^{d-r}; its image is a subdirect bipartite graph on four left and four right vertices. Common bases correspond exactly to three-edge matchings, each lifting in 2^{3(d-r)} ways. At rank two the graph is a perfect matching and has 4 three-edge submatchings; at rank three it is 2-regular, hence C8 or two C4's, and has 16 such matchings; at rank four it is K_4,4 and has C(4,3)^2·3!=96. Comparing these formulas gives the sharp dimensional minima and the disjoint-plane equality condition.

final_claim: For every d≥2 and every pair of three-point subsets of F_2^d, a common three-frequency exponential basis exists; if their direction planes span dimension r∈{2,3,4}, the exact number of unordered common bases is m_r 2^{3(d-r)} with (m_2,m_3,m_4)=(4,16,96), giving the stated sharp minima.
limitations: Pairs of three-point subsets in binary vector spaces only; no result for larger subsets, odd characteristic or general finite abelian groups.
